title: How Stablecoins Go Mainstream | Sergey Nazarov
description:
Chainlink Co-Founder Sergey Nazarov explains why Secure Mint, powered by Chainlink Proof of Reserve, is critical for accelerating global stablecoin adoption. 

Watch the full discussion: https://a-teaminsight.com/thankyou/webinar/?download=74501&submissionGuid=385f9f00-53a7-4410-b9ec-6452532dbc97

Chainlink is the industry-standard oracle platform bringing the capital markets onchain and powering the majority of decentralized finance (DeFi). The Chainlink stack provides the essential data, interoperability, compliance, and privacy standards needed to power advanced blockchain use cases for institutional tokenized assets, lending, payments, stablecoins, and more. Since inventing decentralized oracle networks, Chainlink has enabled tens of trillions in transaction value and now secures the vast majority of DeFi. 

Many of the world’s largest financial services institutions have also adopted Chainlink’s standards and infrastructure, including Swift, Euroclear, Mastercard, Fidelity International, UBS, S&P Dow Jones Indices, FTSE Russell, WisdomTree, ANZ, and top protocols such as Aave, Lido, GMX and many others. Chainlink leverages a novel fee model where offchain and onchain revenue from enterprise adoption is converted to LINK tokens and stored in a strategic Chainlink Reserve. Learn more at chain.link.

✅ Subscribe and turn notifications on: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCnjkrlqaWEBSnKZQ71gdyFA?sub_confirmation=1

Learn more about Chainlink:

Website: https://chain.link
Docs: https://docs.chain.link
Twitter: https://twitter.com/chainlink

#Chainlink #crypto #blockchain

asr.full_text: Paul Carrocaz. So, proof of reserves, from my point of view, is kind of the simplest implementation of a proof of system. There are other proof ofs such as proof of liabilities, proof of solvency. So, there's a whole level or proving what the underlying condition of an asset or an entity is. But proof of reserve simply proves that the assets are there. For example, that the U.S. treasuries are there in the custodian's hands. And the reason to prove it is really twofold. The first reason is that, to Peter's point, if the collateral isn't there, then people are trading in an asset without value. And that would create huge issues for all the people trading in it in the whole industry. The good news is that the availability of the information from custodian APIs is pretty much near real time. So if the custody of the underlying assets changes, I don't even see a reason to do it daily. It could be done every minute every couple of seconds and that produces what's known as the gap. The gap within within fraud circles is the period of time in which fraud can occur. Right the gap of time like for example the Bernie Madoff gap was 20 years. There's a lot of fraud that can happen in 20 years. Enron gap was a little bit shorter because of accounting differences and how accounting works. But essentially you're reducing the gap in which someone can take out capital and use it for something else instead of what it's supposed to be used. The second thing that Peter also mentioned is called secure mint. So secure mint is the ability to actually have the contract that mints the additional stablecoins only be able to mint more stablecoins if there's a verification that there's a corresponding amount of cash. And this avoids scenarios like a recent over-minting scenario where you had the paypal stable coin over minted to 300 trillion u.s dollars and that was because they didn't have secure mint implemented they didn't have anything in the contract in the smart contract that required not only a command from the stablecoin issuer but also a check against the custodian's api so not only are you able to inform the hand from the stable coin issuer, but also a check against the custodians API. So not only are you able to inform the market, but thanks to smart contracts and Oracle systems like Chainlink, you can actually construct the system that makes overminting impossible.
